security.disclaimer: Security checks reduce risk but can't guarantee that a website is safe.
security.ladderBody: Every saved link carries one of these statuses.

PENDING.label: Checking
PENDING.body: The check is running. Publishing and sharing wait for it.

UNKNOWN.label: Not verified
UNKNOWN.body: No provider could vouch for it. You can open it with a warning, and publish or share it once its details are ready (temporary policy).

CLEAR.label: No threats found
CLEAR.body: Can be published and shared. Never a guarantee of safety.

SUSPICIOUS.label: Suspicious
SUSPICIOUS.body: Warning signs found. Not shareable; you can request a review.

MALICIOUS.label: Dangerous
MALICIOUS.body: Known threat. It can't be opened, published or shared.

ai.title: AI that helps you organize — and stays in its lane
ai.body: When enabled on the server, AI reads only public information from the saved page to suggest a summary, tags and a category. It never sees your notes or account details, and it never runs in your browser.

faq.title: Questions
faq.body: Straight answers about privacy, security and sharing.

private.q: Who can see the links I save?
private.a: Only you, until you decide otherwise. You can publish a link (it appears on your profile and in Explore) or invite specific people by e-mail. Your notes are never shown to anyone else.

safe.q: Does “No threats found” mean a site is safe?
safe.a: No. It means the reputation providers didn't know of a threat when the link was checked. It lowers risk but can't guarantee safety, which is why we never label a link “safe”.

ai.a: Only publicly available information from the saved page, such as its title, description and a text excerpt. Private notes, custom edits and account data are never sent. AI can be disabled entirely on the server.

share.a: You invite an e-mail address. The recipient signs in with that verified address and accepts. They get read-only access, and you can revoke it — revoking also removes access for anyone they reshared with.

public.q: Why can't I publish some links?
public.a: Only links whose security check found no threats can be published or shared. Links that are still being checked, couldn't be verified, or were flagged stay private. You can rescan or request a review.

arabic.a: Yes. Search handles Arabic letter variants and diacritics, and English word forms, across titles, descriptions, tags and your notes.

cta.body: Free to start. Private by default.

about.title: About LinkLibrary
about.intro: A bilingual link library for people who collect, research and share what they find on the web.

sections.heading: Why we built it
body: Valuable links get lost in browser tabs, chat threads and notes apps. LinkLibrary gives them a single, organized home with the context you need to use them later.
It was designed for Arabic and English from the start: a full right-to-left interface, and search that understands Arabic text.

sections.heading: What it does
body: Save links privately, let their details be fetched automatically, organize them into collections with tags and categories, and search everything you've saved.
When you're ready, publish individual links or curated collections, or share privately with specific people.

sections.heading: How we approach safety
body: Every destination is checked against threat-intelligence providers before it can be published or shared, and re-checked over time. We are careful with wording: a link with no known threats is shown as “No threats found”, never as “safe”.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: How LinkLibrary handles your information, described as the product works today.

sections.heading: Information you provide
body: Account details: name, username, e-mail address, password (stored hashed), and optionally a bio and profile photo.
Content: the links you save, plus any custom titles, descriptions, tags, categories, notes and collections you create, and the e-mail addresses you invite.

sections.heading: Information processed automatically
body: When you save a link, our servers fetch the page to read publicly available metadata (such as title, description and image) and check the destination with threat-intelligence providers.
We keep session and security records needed to run the service, such as active sessions and an audit log of security-relevant actions.

sections.heading: Optional AI processing
body: If AI enrichment is enabled, publicly available information from saved pages (for example the title, description and an excerpt of the text) may be sent to a third-party AI provider to suggest summaries, categories and tags.
Your private notes, custom edits, invitations and account details are never sent to an AI provider.

sections.heading: Visibility and sharing
body: Links are private by default. A link becomes visible to others only if you publish it or invite specific people. Notes are never shown to anyone else.
Your profile is shown publicly only if you enable the public profile setting.

sections.heading: Your choices
body: You can edit or delete links and collections, revoke sharing, sign out other sessions, change your e-mail and password, and delete your account from Settings.

sections.heading: Cookies
body: The website uses cookies required for signing in and protecting forms (a session cookie and a CSRF-protection cookie), and remembers your language choice. Your theme and layout preferences may be stored in your browser.

sections.heading: Contact
body: Questions about privacy can be sent through the contact page.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: The ground rules for using LinkLibrary, described in plain language.

sections.heading: Your account
body: Keep your password secure and your e-mail address up to date. You are responsible for activity on your account.

sections.heading: Your content
body: You keep ownership of what you save and write. By publishing a link or collection, you choose to make it visible to others through the service.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
body: Don't use the service to distribute malware, phishing or other harmful destinations, to harass people, or to share content you don't have the right to share.
Links flagged by security checks may be restricted, and accounts may be suspended for abuse.

sections.heading: Security checks
body: Security checks reduce risk but cannot guarantee that a website is safe. Use your own judgement before visiting any destination.

sections.heading: Availability
body: Features such as AI suggestions depend on server configuration and third-party providers and may be unavailable at times.

sections.heading: Changes
body: These terms may change as the product evolves. Significant changes will be communicated through the service.
